title.zh: 卷四百十五 列傳第一百七十四 傅伯成 葛洪 曾三復 黃疇若 袁韶 危稹 程公許 羅必元 王遂
title.en: Volume 415 Biographies 174: Fu Bocheng, Ge Hong, Ceng Sanfu, Huang Chouruo, Yuan Shao, Wei Zhen, Cheng Gongxu, Luo Biyuan, Wang Sui
title.raw: 卷四百十五 列傳第一百七十四 傅伯成 葛洪 曾三復 黃疇若 袁韶 危稹 程公許 羅必元 王遂 Volume 415 Biographies 174: Fu Bocheng, Ge Hong, Ceng Sanfu, Huang Chouruo, Yuan Shao, Wei Zhen, Cheng Gongxu, Luo Biyuan, Wang Sui

sentences.zh: 傅伯成葛洪曾三復黃疇若袁韶危稹程公許羅必元王遂

translations.literal: Fu Bocheng, Ge Hong, Ceng Sanfu, Huang Chouruo, Yuan Shao, Wei Zhen, Cheng Gongxu, Luo Biyuan, and Wang Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Fu Bocheng, Ge Hong, Ceng Sanfu, Huang Chouruo, Yuan Shao, Wei Zhen, Cheng Gongxu, Luo Biyuan, and Wang Sui.

sentences.zh: 傅伯成，字景初，吏部員外郎察之孫。

translations.literal: Fu Bocheng, styled Jingchu, was the grandson of Vice Director of Personnel in the Ministry of Officials Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bocheng, whose style was Jingchu, was the grandson of Cai, Vice Director of Personnel in the Ministry of Officials.

sentences.zh: 少從朱熹學。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Zhu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he studied under Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 登隆興元年進士第，調連江尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Longxing and was appointed assistant magistrate of Lianjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the first year of the Longxing reign and was posted as assistant magistrate of Lianjiang.

sentences.zh: 試中教官科，授明州教授。

translations.literal: He passed the instructor examination and was appointed professor at Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the instructor examination, he was appointed professor at Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以年少，嫌以師自居，日與諸生論質往復，後多成才。

translations.literal: Because he was young, he disliked putting on the airs of a teacher; day after day he debated essentials back and forth with the students, and many later became accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling himself too young to play the formal teacher, he debated the substance of learning daily with his students; many of them later rose to distinction.

sentences.zh: 改知閩清縣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as magistrate of Minqing County.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed magistrate of Minqing County.

sentences.zh: 丁父艱，服除，知連江縣。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he entered mourning; when the mourning period ended he was appointed magistrate of Lianjiang County.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he observed the mourning rites, and when they were complete he became magistrate of Lianjiang County.

sentences.zh: 東湖溉田餘二千頃，堤壞。

translations.literal: East Lake irrigated more than two thousand acres of fields, and its dike had collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: East Lake watered more than two thousand acres of farmland, but its dike had broken down.

sentences.zh: 即下流南港為石堤三百尺，民蒙其利。

translations.literal: He immediately built a stone dike three hundred feet long at Nangang on the lower reach, and the people benefited.
translations.idiomatic: He promptly built a three-hundred-foot stone dike at Nangang on the lower reach, to the great benefit of the people.

sentences.zh: 慶元初，召為將作監，進太府寺丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingyuan he was summoned to the Directorate of Imperial Works and promoted to Vice-Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qingyuan era he was called to the Directorate of Imperial Works and soon promoted to Vice-Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 言呂祖儉不當以上書貶。

translations.literal: He memorialized that Lü Zuyijian should not have been demoted for submitting a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that Lü Zuyijian ought not to have been punished with demotion merely for submitting a memorial.

sentences.zh: 又言於御史，朱熹大儒，不可以偽學目之。

translations.literal: He also told the censorate that Zhu Xi was a great Confucian and could not be labeled with the designation of False Learning.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged the censors that Zhu Xi, a leading Confucian scholar, must not be stigmatized as a practitioner of so-called False Learning.

sentences.zh: 又言朋黨之敝，起於人主好惡之偏。

translations.literal: He also said that the harm of factionalism arises from the ruler's partial likes and dislikes.
translations.idiomatic: He further observed that the evils of partisan cliques stem from the sovereign's own partial likes and dislikes.

sentences.zh: 坐是不合，出知漳州，以律己愛民為本。

translations.literal: For this he fell out of favor and was sent out as prefect of Zhangzhou, taking self-discipline and love of the people as his foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Because of these remonstrances he fell from favor and was sent out as prefect of Zhangzhou, where he made strict self-discipline and care for the people his guiding principles.

sentences.zh: 推熹遺意而遵行之，創惠民局，濟民病，以革禨鬼之俗。

translations.literal: He carried out Zhu Xi's surviving intentions, established the Bureau for Benefit to the People to relieve the people's ailments, and reformed the custom of miasma spirits.
translations.idiomatic: He extended Zhu Xi's intentions into practice, founded a Bureau for the People's Welfare to ease popular distress, and worked to uproot superstitious worship of pestilence spirits.

sentences.zh: 由郡南門至漳浦，為橋三十五，治道千二百丈。

translations.literal: From the southern gate of the prefecture to Zhangpu he built thirty-five bridges and repaired twelve hundred zhang of road.
translations.idiomatic: From the prefectural south gate to Zhangpu he built thirty-five bridges and repaired twelve hundred zhang of roadway.

sentences.zh: 兩為部使者，遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Twice he served as a ministry commissioner and was promoted to Vice-Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After serving twice as a ministry commissioner, he was promoted to Vice-Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 時權臣方開邊，語尚秘。

translations.literal: At the time the powerful minister was opening hostilities on the frontier, and policy was still kept secret.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful minister of the day was then pressing for frontier war, and deliberations were still closely guarded.

sentences.zh: 伯成言：“天下之勢，譬如乘舟，中興且八十年矣，外而望之，舟若堅緻，歲月既久，罅漏浸多，苟安旦夕，猶懼覆敗，乃欲徼幸圖古人之所難，臣則未之知也。

translations.literal: Bocheng said: "The condition of the realm is like riding in a boat. The restoration has already lasted nearly eighty years. Viewed from outside, the boat seems solid and tight, but as years pass, cracks and leaks steadily multiply. Contenting oneself with the moment still brings fear of capsizing—yet to hope by luck to attempt what the ancients found difficult is something your servant does not comprehend."
translations.idiomatic: Bocheng said, "The empire is like a vessel underway. Nearly eighty years have passed since the restoration, and from afar the ship still seems sound—but time wears every hull, and leaks spread. To cling to a day's ease while dreading foundering is one thing; to gamble on achieving what even the ancients could scarcely accomplish is quite beyond my understanding."

sentences.zh: ”相府災，同列相率唁丞相，或以為偶然者，伯成正色謂：“天意如此，官師相規時也，以為偶然乎？

translations.literal: When the chief minister's residence burned, his colleagues all went in succession to offer condolences to the chief minister; some regarded it as mere chance. Bocheng said with stern countenance: "Heaven's intent is thus—this is the time for officials and teachers to admonish one another; do you take it for mere chance?"
translations.idiomatic: When fire struck the chief minister's residence, his colleagues hurried to offer condolences; some treated it as mere accident. Bocheng said sternly, "Heaven has sent a sign—this is the moment for ruler and ministers to counsel one another. Can you still call it chance?"

sentences.zh: ”丞相色動。

translations.literal: The chief minister's expression changed.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister's face changed color.

sentences.zh: 遂陳三事：一曰失民心，二曰隳軍政，三曰啟邊釁。

translations.literal: He then set forth three matters: first, loss of the people's hearts; second, ruin of military administration; third, provoking border hostilities.
translations.idiomatic: He then laid out three charges: the loss of popular support, the wrecking of military administration, and the provocation of border conflict.

sentences.zh: 進右司郎官，權幸有私謁者，皆峻拒之。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director in the Right Office; when favorites came with private visits, he sternly refused them all.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Director in the Right Office, he sharply turned away every private caller from among the powerful favorites.

sentences.zh: 出為湖、廣總領。

translations.literal: He was sent out as overall controller for Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was then posted as overall fiscal controller for Huguang.

sentences.zh: 朝議欲納金人之叛降者，伯成言不宜輕棄信誓，乞戒將帥毋生事。

translations.literal: The court debated accepting Jin defectors and deserters. Bocheng said one should not lightly abandon sworn faith and begged that generals be warned not to stir up trouble.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated accepting Jin defectors, Bocheng urged that sworn pledges not be cast aside lightly and asked that commanders be warned against provoking incidents.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞鄧友龍遂劾伯成，罷之。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Deng Youlong thereupon impeached Bocheng and had him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Deng Youlong then impeached Bocheng and secured his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 嘉定元年，召對，麵諭：“前日失於戰，今日失之和。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiading he was summoned for an audience and was told face to face: "Yesterday we erred through war; today we err through peace."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiading he was summoned to audience and told in person, "We erred yesterday by fighting; today we err by suing for peace."

sentences.zh: 小使雖返，要求尚多。

translations.literal: Although the minor envoy has returned, their demands are still many.
translations.idiomatic: Although the junior envoy has returned, the enemy's demands remain numerous.

sentences.zh: 陛下不獲己，悉從之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, having no choice, has acceded to them all.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, left no alternative, has yielded to them all.

sentences.zh: 使和議成，猶可以紓一時之急；

translations.literal: If the peace talks succeed, they may still relieve the urgency of the moment;
translations.idiomatic: If peace can be concluded, it may still ease the immediate crisis;

sentences.zh: 否則虛帑藏以資敵人，驅降附以絕來者，非計也。

translations.literal: otherwise one empties the treasury to supply the enemy and drives away those who surrender and attach themselves, cutting off those who would come—this is no plan.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise the treasury will be drained to enrich the enemy, and those who wish to defect will be driven away—hardly a sound policy.

sentences.zh: 今之策雖以和為主，宜惜日為戰守之備。

translations.literal: Though the present strategy takes peace as its main aim, one should cherish each day to make preparations for war and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Even if peace remains the chief aim, every day should be used to strengthen defenses for war.

sentences.zh: ”權戶部侍郎史彌遠初拜相，麻詞有 “昆命元龜”之語，閩帥倪思以為不當用，御史劾罷思。

translations.literal: Acting Vice-Minister of Revenue Shi Miyuan had just been appointed chief minister; the investiture text contained the phrase "Kunming yuangui." The Fujian commander Ni Si held that it should not have been used, and the censors impeached and dismissed Si.
translations.idiomatic: When Acting Vice-Minister of Revenue Shi Miyuan was first made chief minister, his investiture address used the phrase "Kunming yuangui." Ni Si, commander in Fujian, argued the wording was improper; the censors impeached him and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 伯成因對及其事，帝曰“過當”者再。

translations.literal: In the course of his audience Bocheng brought up this matter, and the emperor twice said it was "excessive."
translations.idiomatic: During his audience Bocheng raised this affair, and the emperor twice called it "going too far."

sentences.zh: 對曰：“思固過當，但恐摧抑太過，遂塞言路，乞明詔台諫侍從，竭盡底蘊，無以思為戒。

translations.literal: He replied: "Si was indeed excessive, but I fear that if suppression goes too far the path of speech will be blocked. I beg that Your Majesty clearly instruct the remonstrance officials and attendants to exhaust their innermost thoughts, and not take Si as a warning."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Ni Si may indeed have overstepped, but I fear that if repression goes too far the avenue of remonstrance will be shut. I beg Your Majesty to issue a clear edict that censors, remonstrators, and attendants should speak their minds fully, and not treat Ni Si as a warning to others."

sentences.zh: ”李壁謫居撫州，伯成言：“侂胄之誅，壁與有功，不酬近功，乃追前罪，他日負罪之臣，不容以功贖過矣。”

translations.literal: Li Bi was demoted and lived in Fuzhou. Bocheng said: "In the execution of Han Tuozhou, Bi had a share in the merit. Not to reward recent merit but instead to pursue past offenses—hereafter guilty ministers will not be allowed to redeem faults by merit."
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi had been banished to Fuzhou. Bocheng said, "Li Bi helped bring about Han Tuozhou's downfall. To ignore his recent service and instead revive old charges means that in future no offender will be allowed to atone through merit."

sentences.zh: 伯成未為諫官也，嚐言：“彌遠謀誅侂胄，事不遂則其家先破，侂胄誅而史代之，勢也。

translations.literal: Before Bocheng became a remonstrance official, he had once said: "Miyuan plotted to execute Tuozhou; if the affair did not succeed his house would be destroyed first. Tuozhou was executed and the Shi family replaced him—such was the momentum of events."
translations.idiomatic: Even before he became a remonstrance official, Bocheng had once remarked, "Miyuan plotted Han Tuozhou's death; had the plot failed, his own house would have perished first. Once Tuozhou fell, the Shi clan took his place—that was the force of circumstance."

sentences.zh: 諸公要相協和，共議國事；

translations.literal: You gentlemen must harmonize with one another and jointly deliberate on state affairs;
translations.idiomatic: You gentlemen must work in harmony and deliberate together on affairs of state;

sentences.zh: 若立黨相擠，必有勝負，非國之福。

translations.literal: if you form factions and squeeze one another, there will surely be winners and losers—this is not the realm's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: if you form factions and tear one another down, victory and defeat will follow—and that is no blessing to the realm.

sentences.zh: ”又勸丞相錢象祖：“安危大事，以死爭之；

translations.literal: He also urged Chief Minister Qian Xiangzu: "On great matters of security and peril, contend unto death;
translations.idiomatic: He also urged Chief Minister Qian Xiangzu, "On matters of national survival, dispute them even at the cost of your life;

sentences.zh: 差除小者，何必乖異？

translations.literal: on minor appointments, why must you be at odds?"
translations.idiomatic: on petty appointments, why need you quarrel?"

sentences.zh: ”拜左諫議大夫，抗疏十有三，皆軍國大義。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Remonstrance Grandee and submitted thirteen forthright memorials, all on great principles of army and state.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Left Remonstrance Grandee, he submitted thirteen forceful memorials, each addressing vital matters of war and state.

sentences.zh: 或致彌遠意，欲使有所彈劾，謂將引以共政。

translations.literal: Someone conveyed Miyuan's wish that he impeach certain persons, saying he would be brought in to share government.
translations.idiomatic: Someone relayed Miyuan's wish that he launch impeachments, promising that he would then be drawn into shared governance.

sentences.zh: 謝之曰：“吾豈傾人以為利哉。

translations.literal: He declined, saying: "How could I overturn others for my own profit?"
translations.idiomatic: He refused, saying, "Would I ruin others for my own gain?"

sentences.zh: ”疏乞詔大臣以公滅私。

translations.literal: In a memorial he begged that great ministers be instructed to subdue private interest by public duty.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he asked that high ministers be charged to let public duty extinguish private interest.

sentences.zh: 左遷權吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was demoted to Acting Vice-Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Acting Vice-Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 以集英殿修撰知建寧府。

translations.literal: As Compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence he was appointed prefect of Jianning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: With the title Compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence, he was made prefect of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 蔡元定謫死道州，歸葬建陽，乃雪其冤於朝。

translations.literal: Cai Yuanding died in banishment at Daozhou and was buried at Jianyang; Bocheng then cleared his wrongful treatment at court.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yuanding had died in exile at Daozhou and was buried at Jianyang; Bocheng then secured the clearing of his name at court.

sentences.zh: 進寶謨閣待制、知鎮江府。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary at the Baomo Pavilion and appointed prefect of Zhenjiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary at the Baomo Pavilion and appointed prefect of Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 全活饑民，瘞藏野殍，不可勝數。

translations.literal: He saved starving people from death, buried abandoned corpses in the fields—their number could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: He kept countless famine victims alive and gave decent burial to unclaimed corpses in the countryside beyond numbering.

sentences.zh: 製置司欲移焦山防江軍於圌山石牌，伯成謂：“虛此實彼，利害等耳。

translations.literal: The Pacification Commission wished to move the Jiaoshan river-defense army to Shipai at Mount Tu. Bocheng said: "To empty this place and strengthen that—the advantage and harm are equal."
translations.idiomatic: The Pacification Commission proposed shifting the Jiaoshan river-defense force to Shipai on Mount Tu. Bocheng objected, "You would weaken one post to strengthen another—the trade is no gain."

sentences.zh: 包港在焦、圌之中，不若兩砦之兵迭戍焉。

translations.literal: Baogang lies between Jiao and Tu; it would be better for the troops of the two forts to garrison it in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Baogang lies between the two posts; better to have both garrisons rotate duty there.

sentences.zh: ”圌山砦兵，素與海盜為地，伯成廉知姓名，會郡都試捕而鞫之，無一逸去。

translations.literal: The troops of Mount Tu fort had long colluded with pirates as their base. Bocheng secretly knew their names; when the prefecture held its triennial examination he seized and interrogated them, and not one escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The Mount Tu garrison had long sheltered pirates; Bocheng knew their names in secret. At the prefecture's triennial examination he had them arrested and interrogated, and not one escaped.

sentences.zh: 獄具，請貸其死，黥隸諸軍。

translations.literal: When the case was complete, he asked that their lives be spared and had them tattooed and enrolled in the armies.
translations.idiomatic: When judgment was rendered, he pleaded for their lives and had them tattooed and assigned to military service.

sentences.zh: 嘉定八年，召赴闕，辭不獲，行至莆，拜疏曰：“臣病不能進矣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiading he was summoned to court; unable to decline, he went as far as Pu, submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant is ill and can go no farther."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Jiading he was summoned to court. Unable to refuse, he traveled as far as Pu and submitted a memorial: "I am too ill to proceed farther."

sentences.zh: ”除寶謨閣直學士、通奉大夫，致仕。

translations.literal: He was appointed Direct Academician at the Baomo Pavilion and Grand Master for Court Audience, and retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the titles Direct Academician at the Baomo Pavilion and Grand Master for Court Audience, and retired from office.

sentences.zh: 理宗即位，升直學士，落致仕，予祠，錫金帶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Lizong took the throne, Bocheng was promoted to Direct Academician, his retirement was annulled, he was granted a temple stipend, and presented with a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Lizong ascended the throne, Bocheng was promoted to Direct Academician, recalled from retirement, granted a temple stipend, and awarded a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 伯成辭免，乃進“昭明天常、扶持人極”之說，詔進一官。

translations.literal: Bocheng declined; he then advanced the doctrine of "making clear Heaven's constant way and upholding the human pole," and an edict promoted him one rank.
translations.idiomatic: Bocheng declined the honors but presented his doctrine on clarifying Heaven's constant way and upholding the human pole; an edict advanced him one rank.

sentences.zh: 寶慶元年，與楊簡同召，尋加寶文閣學士，提舉佑神觀，奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baqing he was summoned together with Yang Jian; shortly thereafter he was made Academician at the Baowen Pavilion, Superintendent of the Youshen Observatory, and Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baqing he was summoned together with Yang Jian, then made Academician at the Baowen Pavilion, Superintendent of the Youshen Observatory, and Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 雖力以老病辭，而愛君憂國之念不少衰。

translations.literal: Although he strenuously declined on grounds of age and illness, his devotion to the ruler and concern for the state did not diminish in the least.
translations.idiomatic: Though he pleaded age and illness to decline office, his love for the ruler and anxiety for the state scarcely waned.

sentences.zh: 聞大理評事胡夢昱坐論事貶，蹙然語所親曰：“向呂祖儉之謫，吾為小臣，猶嚐抗論。

translations.literal: Hearing that Hu Mengyu, Evaluator at the Court of Judicial Review, was demoted for discussing state affairs, he knit his brows and said to those close to him: "When Lü Zuyijian was demoted, I was a minor official yet still ventured forthright argument."
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Hu Mengyu of the Court of Judicial Review had been banished for remonstrating on public affairs, he frowned and told his intimates, "When Lü Zuyijian was banished, I was only a junior official, yet I still spoke out boldly."

sentences.zh: 今蒙國恩，叨竊至此而不言，誰當言者。

translations.literal: Now, having received the state's grace and presumptuously risen to this position yet remaining silent—who should speak if not I?
translations.idiomatic: Now, favored by the state and risen to this rank, if I remain silent, who else will speak?

sentences.zh: ”遂抗疏曰：“臣恐陛下不復聞天下事矣。

translations.literal: He then submitted a forthright memorial saying: "Your servant fears that Your Majesty will no longer hear of affairs under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a forceful memorial: "I fear Your Majesty will no longer hear what is happening in the realm."

sentences.zh: 方今內無良吏，田裏怨谘，外無名將，邊陲危急，而廉恥道喪，風俗益偷，賄賂流行，公私俱困。

translations.literal: At present within there are no good officials and the fields murmur with complaint; without there are no renowned generals and the frontiers are in peril. The way of integrity and shame is lost, customs grow ever more dissolute, bribery spreads, and public and private alike are distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Within, there are no worthy officials and the countryside seethes with grievance; without, there are no distinguished generals and the borders stand in peril. Integrity has collapsed, morals grow lax, bribery runs rampant, and both state and people are exhausted.

sentences.zh: 謂宜君臣上下，憂邊恤民，以弭禍亂。

translations.literal: He said ruler and ministers above and below should worry over the borders and care for the people to quell calamity and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Ruler and ministers alike, he urged, should fret over the frontiers and care for the people to avert disaster.

sentences.zh: 奈何今日某人言某事，未幾而斥，明日某人言某事，未幾而斥，則是上疏者以共工、兜之刑加之矣。

translations.literal: Yet today when someone speaks on some matter, before long he is dismissed; tomorrow when someone speaks on some matter, before long he is dismissed—then those who submit memorials are punished with the penalties of Gonggong and Dou.
translations.idiomatic: Yet today one man speaks on a matter and is soon dismissed; tomorrow another speaks and is likewise dismissed—so that memorialists are punished as Gonggong and Dou were of old.

sentences.zh: 昔韓愈論後世人主奉佛，運祚短促，唐憲宗大怒，將抵以死，自崔群、裴度戚裏諸賢皆為愈言，止貶潮州，尋復內徙。

translations.literal: Formerly Han Yu argued that later rulers who honored Buddhism had short reigns. Emperor Xianzong of Tang was greatly angered and was about to punish him with death; from Cui Qun and Pei Du to worthy men among the imperial kin, all spoke for Yu, and he was only banished to Chaozhou, soon afterward recalled inland.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Han Yu warned that rulers who embraced Buddhism shortened their dynasties. Emperor Xianzong of Tang was furious and nearly had him executed; but Cui Qun, Pei Du, and other worthy men at court pleaded for him, and he was merely banished to Chaozhou, then soon recalled inland.

sentences.zh: 今上疏者非可愈比，然在列之臣，無一為言者，萬一死於瘴癘，陛下與大臣有殺諫者之謗，史冊書之，有累聖治。

translations.literal: Today's memorialist cannot be compared with Yu, yet among the officials in attendance not one speaks for him. If by mischance he dies of miasma, Your Majesty and the great ministers will bear the reproach of having killed a remonstrator; the historical records will inscribe it, to the detriment of sagely rule.
translations.idiomatic: Today's petitioner is no Han Yu, yet not one minister at court speaks for him. Should he die of southern pestilence, Your Majesty and your ministers will bear the stigma of silencing a remonstrator; the annals will record it to the harm of your reign.

sentences.zh: 臣垂盡之年，與斯人相去，風馬牛之不相及，獨以受恩優異，效其瞽言。

translations.literal: Your servant, in the waning years of life, is far removed from this man—their courses like wind, horse, and ox, never meeting—yet solely because he has received exceptional grace, he offers his blind words.
translations.idiomatic: I am in my final years and have nothing to do with this man—our paths could scarcely cross—yet because the state has favored me beyond desert, I offer these imperfect words.

sentences.zh: ”不報。

translations.literal: There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: He received no answer.

sentences.zh: 明年，加龍圖閣學士，轉一官，提舉鴻慶宮，復辭。

translations.literal: The following year he was made Academician at the Longtu Pavilion, advanced one rank, appointed Superintendent of the Hongqing Palace, and again declined.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made Academician at the Longtu Pavilion, advanced one rank, appointed Superintendent of the Hongqing Palace, and declined once more.

sentences.zh: 伯成純實無妄，表裏洞達，每稱人善，不啻如己出，語及奸人誤國，邪人害正，詞色俱厲，不少假借，常慕屍諫，疏草畢，亟命繕寫，朝服而逝，年八十有四。

translations.literal: Bocheng was pure, sincere, and without pretense; inside and out he was transparent. He always praised others' virtues as if they were his own. When he spoke of traitors who misled the state or wicked men who harmed the upright, both word and countenance grew stern, and he made no concession. He often admired dying remonstrance; when a memorial draft was finished he urgently ordered it copied, donned court robes, and passed away, aged eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Bocheng was plain, sincere, and without artifice, transparent in word and deed. He praised others' virtues as warmly as his own. When traitors who misled the state or wicked men who harmed the upright were mentioned, his words and bearing turned fierce, and he yielded nothing. He admired the ideal of remonstrating unto death; when a memorial was finished he had it copied at once, put on his court robes, and died, aged eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Palace with the insignia of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted the title Grand Master of the Palace with the insignia of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 端平三年，賜諡忠簡。

translations.literal: In the third year of Duanping he was granted the posthumous title Zhongjian (Loyal and Simple).
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Duanping he was given the posthumous epithet Loyal and Plain.

sentences.zh: 葛洪，字容父，婺州東陽人。

translations.literal: Ge Hong, styled Rongfu, was a native of Dongyang in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong, whose style was Rongfu, came from Dongyang in Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 從呂祖謙學，登淳熙十一年進士第。

translations.literal: He studied under Lü Zuqian and passed the jinshi examination in the eleventh year of Chunxi.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Lü Zuqian and earned his jinshi degree in the eleventh year of the Chunxi reign.

sentences.zh: 嘉定間，為樞密院編修官兼國史院編修官、實錄院檢討官。

translations.literal: During the Jiading era he served as Compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs, concurrently Compiler at the Bureau of National History and Reviser at the Veritable Records Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiading era he served as compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs, concurrently compiler at the Bureau of National History and reviser at the Veritable Records Bureau.

sentences.zh: 遷守尚書工部員外郎兼權樞密院檢詳諸房文字。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Works in the Department of State Affairs, concurrently Acting Examiner of Documents in the Various Offices of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Works and concurrently served as acting examiner of documents in the various offices of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 上疏言：

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 今之將帥，其才與否，臣不得而盡知。

translations.literal: As for today's generals and commanders, whether they have talent or not, your servant cannot know them all.
translations.idiomatic: As for today's commanders, I cannot know the full measure of each man's ability.

sentences.zh: 惟忠誠所在，凡為人臣者斯須所不可離，則不可不以是責之耳。

translations.literal: Only loyalty is what no subject may depart from for a moment; therefore they cannot but be held to this standard.
translations.idiomatic: But loyalty is what no subject may abandon for an instant, and on that score they must be held accountable.

sentences.zh: 今安居無事，非必奮不顧死，冒水火，蹈白刃，而後謂之忠也。

translations.literal: Now, dwelling in peace without incident, one need not necessarily throw oneself into fire and water or tread bare blades before it is called loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: In times of peace one need not rush through fire or face naked blades to prove loyalty.

sentences.zh: 第職思其憂謂之忠，公爾忘私謂之忠，純實不欺謂之忠。

translations.literal: Merely to think of one's duties in anxiety is called loyalty; to be public-minded and forget private interest is called loyalty; to be pure, sincere, and without deceit is called loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: To dwell on one's duties with care is loyalty; to set public good above private gain is loyalty; to be honest and without deceit is loyalty.

sentences.zh: 且拊循士卒，帥之職也，朝廷每嚴掊克之禁，蠲營運之逋，其儆之者至矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, comforting and guiding the troops is a commander's duty; the court has repeatedly strictly forbidden extortion and remitted arrears on transport levies—the warnings have been utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Comforting and guiding the troops is a commander's duty, and the court has repeatedly forbidden extortion and remitted transport arrears—the warnings could scarcely be sterner.

sentences.zh: 今乃有別為名色，益肆貪黷，視生理之稍豐者而誣以非辜，動輒估籍，擇廩給之稍優者而強以庫務，取辦芻粟，抑配軍需，於拊循何有哉！

translations.literal: Yet now there are those who invent separate categories and indulge greed all the more; they see those whose livelihoods are somewhat ample and falsely charge them with crimes, at every turn seizing property by appraisal and registration; they select those whose grain rations are somewhat better and force them into treasury duties, requisitioning fodder and grain and compulsorily allocating military supplies—what comfort and guidance is there in this!
translations.idiomatic: Yet some invent new pretexts for ever greater graft: they target anyone modestly prosperous with false charges, seize property through forced appraisals, press men with better rations into treasury labor, and extort fodder and supplies—this is comfort for the troops?

sentences.zh: 訓齊戎旅，亦帥之職也，朝廷每嚴點試之法，申階級之令，其儆之亦切矣。

translations.literal: Drilling and ordering the army is also a commander's duty; the court has repeatedly enforced strict inspection laws and reiterated orders on ranks—the warnings have been keen as well.
translations.idiomatic: Drilling and disciplining the troops is likewise a commander's duty, and the court has repeatedly tightened inspection rules and rank regulations—the admonitions have been equally stern.

sentences.zh: 今顧有教閱視為具文，坐作僅同兒戲，技勇者不與旌賞，拙懦者未嚐勸懲，士日橫驕，類難役使，於訓齊何有哉

translations.literal: Yet now some treat military instruction and review as empty form; sitting and rising are barely more than child's play; the skilled and brave receive no commendation or reward, while the clumsy and timid are never encouraged or punished; the soldiers grow daily arrogant and insubordinate, and are mostly hard to employ—what drilling and ordering is there in this?
translations.idiomatic: Yet some treat training reviews as mere paperwork, drills as child's play, reward the brave never, and discipline the inept never; the men grow daily arrogant and unruly—where is the discipline in that?

sentences.zh: 況乃有沉酣聲色之奉，溺意田宅之圖，而不恤國事者矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, there are those sunk deep in the pleasures of music and beauty, drowning their minds in schemes for fields and houses, who do not care for state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Worse still are those lost in music and courtesans, obsessed with land and property, and indifferent to affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 又有營營終日，專務納交，書幣往來，道路旁午，而妄希升進者矣。

translations.literal: There are also those who bustle all day long, devoted solely to cultivating connections; letters and gifts pass back and forth and the roads are crowded at noon, while they vainly hope for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Others bustle all day cultivating connections, letters and gifts crowding the roads, while they dream of promotion.

sentences.zh: 自謂繕治器甲，修造戰艦，究其實，則飾舊為新而已爾。

translations.literal: They claim to repair armor and weapons and build warships, but when examined in fact it is merely refurbishing the old as new.
translations.idiomatic: They claim to repair arms and build warships, but in truth merely dress up old gear as new.

sentences.zh: 自謂撙節財用，聲稱羨餘，原其自，則剝下罔上而已爾。

translations.literal: They claim to economize expenditures and boast of surplus, but tracing it to its source it is merely stripping those below and deceiving those above.
translations.idiomatic: They claim thrift and report surpluses, but at bottom they merely squeeze the ranks and deceive their superiors.

sentences.zh: 乞嚴飭將帥，上下振厲，申致軍實，常若有寇至之憂。

translations.literal: I beg that generals and commanders be strictly admonished, that above and below be roused and invigorated, that military substance be brought to fulfillment, and that there always be concern as if the enemy were about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that commanders be strictly disciplined, that the whole army be roused, that military readiness be restored, and that all live as though the enemy were at the gates.

sentences.zh: 磨礪振刷，以求更新，亦庶乎其有用矣。

translations.literal: Grind and polish, rouse and refresh, seeking renewal—then perhaps they may prove useful.
translations.idiomatic: If they are honed and renewed, they may yet prove of some use.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 進直煥章閣，為國子祭酒，仍兼國史編修、實錄檢討。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Direct Attendant at the Huanzhang Pavilion, appointed Director of the National University, and still concurrently served as Compiler of the National History and Reviser of the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Direct Attendant at the Huanzhang Pavilion and made Director of the National University, while retaining his posts as compiler of the national history and reviser of the veritable records.

sentences.zh: 遷工部侍郎，仍兼祭酒兼同修國史實錄院同修撰，拜工部尚書，亦兼祭酒兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice-Minister of Works, still concurrently Director of the National University and Associate Compiler at the Bureau of National History and Veritable Records; he was then appointed Minister of Works, also concurrently Director of the National University and Lecturer-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice-Minister of Works while retaining the directorship of the National University and an associate compilership at the national history and veritable records bureau; later he was appointed Minister of Works, still directing the National University and serving as lecturer-in-attendance.

sentences.zh: 進端明殿學士、同簽書樞密院事，拜參知政事，封東陽郡公。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Academician at the Duanming Hall and Concurrent Signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, appointed Vice Grand Councilor, and enfeoffed as Duke of Dongyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Academician at the Duanming Hall and concurrent signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, appointed vice grand councilor, and enfeoffed as Duke of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 讚討平李全，援王素諫仁宗卻王德用進女事，以止備嬪禦，世多稱之。

translations.literal: He praised the campaign to suppress Li Quan and cited Wang Su's remonstrance to Emperor Renzong rejecting Wang Deyong's presentation of a daughter, to stop the selection of reserve consorts—later generations widely praised this.
translations.idiomatic: He commended the suppression of Li Quan and cited Wang Su's remonstrance against Emperor Renzong's acceptance of Wang Deyong's daughter, thereby halting the filling of the inner quarters—an act widely praised by later generations.

sentences.zh: 以資政殿學士、提舉洞霄宮，進大學士。

translations.literal: As Academician at the Hall for Assisting Governance and Superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace, he was advanced to Grand Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as Academician at the Hall for Assisting Governance and superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace, he was advanced to Grand Academician.

sentences.zh: 召赴行在，仍舊職充萬壽觀使兼侍讀，尋提舉萬壽觀兼侍讀，守本官致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the traveling court, retained his former post as Superintendent of the Wanshou Observatory while also serving as Lecturer-in-Attendance, soon became Superintendent of the Wanshou Observatory concurrently Lecturer-in-Attendance, retired while holding his original rank, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the traveling court, he resumed his old duties as superintendent of the Wanshou Observatory and lecturer-in-attendance, later held both posts together, retired at his original rank, and died.

sentences.zh: 帝輟視朝一日，諡端獻。

translations.literal: The emperor suspended court audiences for one day and granted him the posthumous title Duansian (Correct and Offering).
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspended court for a day in mourning and gave him the posthumous epithet Correct and Offering.

sentences.zh: 杜範稱其侃侃守正，有大臣風。

translations.literal: Du Fan praised him as easy and upright in bearing, with the manner of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: Du Fan praised his easy dignity and steadfast integrity, calling it the bearing of a true statesman.

sentences.zh: 有奏議、雜著文二十四卷。

translations.literal: He left twenty-four juan of memorials and miscellaneous writings.
translations.idiomatic: His collected memorials and miscellaneous writings filled twenty-four juan.

sentences.zh: 曾三復字無玷，臨江人。

translations.literal: Ceng Sanfu, styled Wudian, was a native of Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Ceng Sanfu, whose style was Wudian, came from Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 乾道六年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Qiandao.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the sixth year of the Qiandao reign.

sentences.zh: 淳熙末，為主管官告院，遷太府寺簿，曆將作、太府丞。

translations.literal: At the end of Chunxi he served as supervisor of the Bureau of Official Commissions, was transferred to Registrar of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, and successively served as Vice-Director at the Directorate of Imperial Works and the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Chunxi era he supervised the Bureau of Official Commissions, then served as registrar of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and subsequently as vice-director at both the Directorate of Imperial Works and the Court of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 登朝數年，安於平進，搢紳稱之。

translations.literal: After several years at court he was content with steady advancement, and the gentry praised him.
translations.idiomatic: After several years at court he was content with steady promotion, and the official class spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 紹熙初，出知池州，改常州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaoxi he was sent out as prefect of Chizhou and then transferred to Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaoxi era he was posted prefect of Chizhou, then transferred to Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 召為御史檢法，拜監察御史，轉太常少卿，進起居舍人，遷起居郎兼權刑部侍郎，以疾告老。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Examiner of Law for the Censorate, appointed Investigating Censor, transferred to Vice-Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, promoted to Recorder of the Emperor's Movements, then transferred to Attendant Recorder concurrently Acting Vice-Minister of Justice, and retired on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as legal examiner for the censorate, he became investigating censor, then vice-director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, recorder of the emperor's movements, and attendant recorder with acting rank as vice-minister of justice before retiring on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 詔守本官職致仕。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to retire while retaining his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: An edict permitted him to retire while keeping his original rank.

sentences.zh: 三復性耿介，恥奔競，故位不速進。

translations.literal: Sanfu's nature was upright and unyielding; he was ashamed of scrambling for advancement, and therefore his rank did not rise quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Sanfu was upright by nature and despised office-seeking, so his promotions came slowly.

sentences.zh: 在台餘兩年，持論正平，不隨不激。

translations.literal: He remained at the Censorate for more than two years, holding his arguments level and fair, neither following others nor being provocative.
translations.idiomatic: At the censorate for more than two years, his opinions were even-handed—neither partisan nor inflammatory.

sentences.zh: 其沒也，士論惜之。

translations.literal: At his death, scholarly opinion regretted his loss.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, men of learning mourned the loss.

sentences.zh: 黃疇若，字伯庸，隆興豐城人。

translations.literal: Huang Chouruo, styled Boyong, was a native of Fengcheng in Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chouruo, whose style was Boyong, came from Fengcheng in Longxing.

sentences.zh: 一歲而孤，外大母杜教之。

translations.literal: He was orphaned at one year; his maternal grandmother Du raised and taught him.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at the age of one, he was raised and taught by his maternal grandmother, Lady Du.

sentences.zh: 淳熙五年舉進士，授祁陽縣主簿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunxi he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk of Qiyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Chunxi and was appointed chief clerk of Qiyang County.

sentences.zh: 邑民有訴僧為盜且殺人，移鞫治，疇若疑其無證，以白提點刑獄馬大同，且爭之甚力，已而得真盜，大同薦之，調柳州教授，又調靈川令。

translations.literal: A townsman accused a monk of robbery and murder; the case was transferred for interrogation. Chouruo doubted there was evidence, reported this to Judicial Intendant Ma Datong, and argued the point strenuously. Later the real robber was caught; Datong recommended him, and he was transferred to professor at Liuzhou and then magistrate of Lingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: When locals accused a monk of robbery and murder, Chouruo doubted the evidence, reported his suspicions to Judicial Intendant Ma Datong, and argued the case forcefully. The real culprit was later caught; Datong recommended him, and he was posted professor at Liuzhou, then magistrate of Lingchuan.

sentences.zh: 會萬安軍黎蠻竊發，經略司選疇若條畫招捕事宜。

translations.literal: When Li tribesmen in Wan'an Circuit rose in secret revolt, the Pacification Commission selected Chouruo to draft plans for summons and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: When Li tribesmen in Wan'an Circuit rebelled, the Pacification Commission chose Chouruo to draft plans for their pacification.

sentences.zh: 疇若謂須稽原始亂，為區處之方。

translations.literal: Chouruo said one must investigate the original causes of the disorder and devise measures for handling it.
translations.idiomatic: Chouruo argued that the roots of the unrest must be traced before remedies could be devised.

sentences.zh: 再任嶺外，用舉考改知廬陵縣。

translations.literal: After a second term beyond the mountains, through recommendation and evaluation he was transferred to serve as magistrate of Luling County.
translations.idiomatic: After a second posting in the far south, he was recommended and made magistrate of Luling County.

sentences.zh: 州常以六月督畸零稅，疇若念民方艱食，取任內縣用錢三十餘緡為民代輸兩年。

translations.literal: The prefecture regularly in the sixth month pressed collection of scattered residual taxes. Chouruo, mindful that the people were in hard straits for food, took more than thirty strings of the county's operating funds from his tenure to pay on their behalf for two years.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture habitually collected scattered residual taxes in the sixth month. Mindful that the people were starving, Chouruo used more than thirty strings of county funds to pay these taxes for them for two years.

sentences.zh: 諸司舉為邑最官，召赴都堂審察，差監行在都進奏院。

translations.literal: Various offices recommended him as the outstanding county official; he was summoned to the chief council chamber for examination and appointed supervisor of the Capital Memorial Transmission Office at the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as the outstanding county magistrate, he was summoned for review at the chief council chamber and appointed supervisor of the capital memorial transmission office.

sentences.zh: 開禧元年，都城火。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaixi the capital city caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaixi fire broke out in the capital.

sentences.zh: 疇若應詔上言曰：“當今之急務有三：一曰賦斂征求之無藝，二曰都鄙軍民之無法，三曰守令牧養之無狀。

translations.literal: Chouruo responded to the edict with a memorial saying: "The urgent tasks of the present are three: first, taxation and exaction without limit; second, capital and countryside, army and people without law; third, prefects and magistrates who nurture without proper conduct."
translations.idiomatic: Chouruo memorialized in response: "Three tasks are urgent today: unchecked taxation and exaction; lawlessness in the capital and the provinces, among soldiers and civilians alike; and magistrates who fail in their duty to care for the people."

sentences.zh: ”遷太府寺主簿，又遷將作監丞兼皇弟吳興郡王府教授。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, then to Vice-Director of the Directorate of Imperial Works concurrently Professor at the mansion of the emperor's younger brother, Prince of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief clerk of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, then vice-director of the Directorate of Imperial Works and professor at the mansion of the emperor's younger brother, Prince of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 遷太府寺丞，又遷秘書丞兼權禮部郎官，兼資善堂說書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice-Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, then to Vice-Director of the Secretariat concurrently Acting Director in the Ministry of Rites, and Lecturer at the Hall for Cultivating Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice-director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, then vice-director of the Secretariat with acting rank in the Ministry of Rites, and lecturer at the Hall for Cultivating Goodness.

sentences.zh: 遷著作郎，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Compiler and appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He became a compiler, then investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 首章乞天子擇宰相，宰相擇監司。

translations.literal: In his first memorial he begged that the Son of Heaven choose the chief minister, and the chief minister choose the circuit intendants.
translations.idiomatic: In his opening memorial he urged the emperor to choose the chief minister wisely, and the chief minister to choose circuit intendants wisely.

sentences.zh: 又言：“善為國者必以恐懼修省之訓陳於前，善為相者必以危亡災異之事告於上。”

translations.literal: He also said: "One who governs the state well must set forth lessons of fear and self-examination; one who serves as chief minister well must report matters of peril, ruin, and strange omens to his superiors."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "A good ruler keeps lessons of fear and self-examination always before him; a good minister keeps warnings of peril and strange omens always before his sovereign."

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄敗，畤若上章丐去，帝批其奏曰：“卿懷忠藎，朕固知之。

translations.literal: When Han Tuozhou fell, Chouruo submitted a memorial begging to leave office. The emperor annotated his memorial: "You harbor loyal devotion—I have long known it."
translations.idiomatic: After Han Tuozhou's fall, Chouruo asked to resign. The emperor wrote on his memorial, "Your loyal devotion I have always known."

sentences.zh: ”疇若遂疏鄧友龍、陳景俊之惡。

translations.literal: Chouruo then memorialized exposing the wickedness of Deng Youlong and Chen Jingjun.
translations.idiomatic: Chouruo then exposed the crimes of Deng Youlong and Chen Jingjun in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 先是，江、淮督府既罔功，罷不更置。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Jiang-Huai command headquarters, having achieved nothing, was abolished and not re-established.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Jiang-Huai command headquarters had accomplished nothing and was abolished without replacement.

sentences.zh: 疇若奏，以為和戰未決，不遣近臣置幕府，無以統諸將。

translations.literal: Chouruo memorialized that since peace and war were undecided, without sending a close minister to establish a headquarters there was no way to command the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Chouruo argued that with peace and war still unsettled, no close minister had been sent to establish a headquarters, leaving no one to command the generals.

sentences.zh: 乞檢會前奏，亟詔大臣科條人才為宣撫使。

translations.literal: He begged that previous memorials be reviewed and that the court urgently order great ministers to assess talent and appoint a pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that earlier memorials be reviewed and that ministers be ordered at once to select a pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 帝即日以丘崈為江、淮製置使。

translations.literal: That very day the emperor appointed Qiu Jun Pacification Commissioner for Jiang and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the emperor appointed Qiu Jun pacification commissioner for Jiang and Huai.

sentences.zh: 尋遷疇若殿中侍御史兼侍講。

translations.literal: Soon Chouruo was transferred to Palace Censor concurrently Court Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chouruo was made palace censor and court lecturer.

sentences.zh: 朝廷與金人約和，金人約函致侂胄首。

translations.literal: The court made peace with the Jurchens, who stipulated that Tuozhou's head be sent in a box.
translations.idiomatic: The court made peace with the Jin, who demanded Tuozhou's head be sent in a casket.

sentences.zh: 詔令台諫、侍從、兩省雜議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the censors, remonstrators, attendants, and officials of both provincial secretariats to discuss the matter jointly.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered censors, attendants, and officials of both secretariats to deliberate jointly.

sentences.zh: 疇若與章燮等奏：“ 乞梟首，然後函送敵國。

translations.literal: Chouruo and Zhang Xie and others memorialized: "We beg that the head be displayed first, and only then sent in a box to the enemy state."
translations.idiomatic: Chouruo, Zhang Xie, and others memorialized, "We ask that the head be displayed publicly before it is sent to the enemy in a casket."

sentences.zh: ”人譏其有失國體。

translations.literal: People ridiculed this as damaging to national dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said this compromised the dignity of the state.

sentences.zh: 疇若奏：“今帑藏無餘，歲幣若必睥睨於百姓，願自宮禁以及宰執百官共為撙節，逐年樁積。

translations.literal: Chouruo memorialized: "The treasury now has no surplus. If the annual tribute must be squeezed from the common people, I wish that from the inner palace to the chief ministers and all officials alike we practice economy and accumulate year by year."
translations.idiomatic: Chouruo memorialized, "The treasury is empty. If the annual tribute must be wrung from the people, let the palace, the chief ministers, and all officials practice thrift and build reserves year by year."

sentences.zh: ”遂置安邊所。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Bureau for Pacifying the Frontier was established.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau for Pacifying the Frontier was then established.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎沈詵條具合節省拘催者，疇若復乞：“依仁宗、孝宗兩朝成訓，凡節省事：在內諸司選內侍長一員，令自行搜訪，條具來上；

translations.literal: Vice-Minister of Revenue Shen Shen listed items suitable for economizing and collection. Chouruo again begged: "Following the established instructions of the Renzong and Xiaozong reigns, for all matters of economy: within the palace bureaus select one senior eunuch to investigate on his own and submit a detailed list;
translations.idiomatic: Vice-Minister of Revenue Shen Shen listed items for economizing. Chouruo again asked that, following the precedents of Emperors Renzong and Xiaozong, each inner bureau choose a senior eunuch to investigate and report;

sentences.zh: 在外廷三省則委宰掾、樞屬，六曹則委長貳，事幹浮費者聞奏。

translations.literal: in the outer court entrust the three secretariats' chief clerks and bureau of military affairs staff, and the six ministries' senior and junior directors; matters involving wasteful expenditure are to be reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: in the outer court entrust the secretariats' chief clerks and military bureau staff, and the ministries' senior officers; wasteful expenditures should be reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: ”又乞：“以官司房廊及激賞庫四季所獻並侂胄萬畝莊等，一並拘樁。

translations.literal: He also begged: "Let official buildings and corridors, the seasonal offerings of the Commendation Treasury, and Tuozhou's ten-thousand-mu estates and the like all be seized and registered."
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that official properties, the Commendation Treasury's seasonal offerings, and Tuozhou's vast estates all be seized and registered.

sentences.zh: ”既而內廷及酒所減省，議多格，獨得估籍奸賊及房廊非泛供須五項，總緡錢九百一十三萬有奇，外樁留產業，每歲又可得七十一萬五千三百餘緡，疇若乞：“令後省類聚更化以來臣下章奏，察其可行者以聞，付之中書。”

translations.literal: Later, reductions in the inner court and wine offices were mostly blocked in deliberation; only five items were obtained—appraised registration of traitors and thieves, and corridors for non-routine supplies—totaling more than nine million thirteen thousand strings; besides registered retained properties, each year another seventy-one thousand five hundred and more strings could be obtained. Chouruo begged: "Let the Secretariat gather memorials of subjects since the renewal of rule, examine those feasible, report them, and refer them to the Secretariat-Chancellery."
translations.idiomatic: Later, proposed cuts in the inner court and wine offices were mostly blocked; only five measures succeeded—seizing traitors' assets and nonessential properties—yielding over nine million strings, with annual income of another seventy-one thousand strings from retained estates. Chouruo asked that memorials since the reform be collected, viable proposals reported, and referred to the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 都城穀踴貴，詔減價糶樁管米十萬石，於是淮、浙流民交集。

translations.literal: Grain in the capital soared in price; an edict ordered the sale at reduced price of one hundred thousand shi of stored rice, whereupon refugees from Huai and Zhe converged.
translations.idiomatic: When grain prices in the capital soared, an edict ordered the sale of one hundred thousand shi of reserve rice at reduced prices, drawing refugees from Huai and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 臨安府按籍振濟，僅不滿五千人，以三月後麥熟罷振濟，各給糧遣歸。

translations.literal: Lin'an Prefecture relieved according to registers barely fewer than five thousand people; after the third month, when wheat ripened, relief was ended and each was given grain and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Lin'an Prefecture registered fewer than five thousand for relief; when wheat ripened in the third month, relief ended and each refugee was given grain and sent home.

sentences.zh: 疇若謂：“ 此實驅之使去耳。

translations.literal: Chouruo said: "This is in truth driving them away."
translations.idiomatic: Chouruo said, "This amounts to driving them away."

sentences.zh: ”遂奏：“乞令核實，近甸之人，願歸就田者勿問，其有未能歸者，更振濟兩月；

translations.literal: He then memorialized: "I beg that verification be ordered. For those in the near suburbs who wish to return to their fields, do not hinder them; for those unable to return, extend relief two months more;"
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "Verify the registers: let suburban refugees who wish to return to their fields go freely; extend relief two months for those who cannot yet return;"

sentences.zh: 淮民見在都城者，其家既破，又無贏貲，必難遽去，仍與振恤，俟早熟乃罷。

translations.literal: for Huai people now in the capital, their families already ruined and without surplus funds, it will surely be hard to leave quickly—still grant them relief and wait until early crops ripen before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Huai refugees in the capital, their homes ruined and without savings, cannot leave quickly—continue relief until the early harvest.

sentences.zh: ”於是詔振濟至六月乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered that relief continue until the sixth month before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then extended relief until the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 帝以蝗災，令刺舉監司不才者，疇若同台監考察上之。

translations.literal: Because of locust disaster the emperor ordered impeachment of incompetent circuit intendants; Chouruo together with the censorate investigated and reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: After locust plagues, the emperor ordered incompetent circuit intendants impeached; Chouruo joined the censorate in investigating and reporting them.

sentences.zh: 又言：“湖、廣盜賊，固迫於饑寒，然亦有激而成之者。

translations.literal: He also said: "Bandits in Hunan and Guang are indeed driven by hunger and cold, yet some are also provoked into becoming such."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Bandits in Hunan and Guangdong are driven by hunger and cold, but some are provoked into rebellion."

sentences.zh: 黑風峒寇，實由官不為決訟所致。

translations.literal: The bandits of Heifeng Cave were in truth caused by officials who would not decide lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: The Heifeng Cave bandits arose because officials refused to settle lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 宜戒湖、廣諸司，申明法禁為賊，關防以時，平心決訟，勿令砦官巡尉侵漁。

translations.literal: The various offices of Hunan and Guang should be warned to clarify legal prohibitions against becoming bandits, guard passes in season, decide lawsuits impartially, and not let fort officials and patrol inspectors plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Offices in Hunan and Guangdong should be warned to enforce laws against banditry, guard passes properly, judge fairly, and stop fort officials and patrol inspectors from extorting the people.

sentences.zh: ”權戶部侍郎，金使告主亡，差充館伴。

translations.literal: He was Acting Vice-Minister of Revenue; when the Jin envoy reported his sovereign's death, Chouruo was appointed to serve as host commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: As acting vice-minister of revenue, he was appointed host commissioner when the Jin envoy reported his emperor's death.

sentences.zh: 自軍興費廣，朝廷給會子數多，至是折閱日甚。

translations.literal: Since the outbreak of war expenses were vast and the court issued many huizi notes; by this time depreciation grew daily worse.
translations.idiomatic: War had swollen expenses and the court had issued vast quantities of paper notes; by now their value was collapsing daily.

sentences.zh: 朝論頗嚴稱提，民愈不售，郡縣科配，民皆閉門牢避。

translations.literal: Court opinion strongly favored strict maintenance of note value; the people were ever less willing to accept them, and when prefectures and counties apportioned them, the people all shut their doors and firmly avoided them.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion favored strict enforcement of note value, but the people refused them ever more; when counties apportioned them by quota, people barred their doors to avoid receiving them.

sentences.zh: 行旅持券，終日有不獲一錢一物者。

translations.literal: Travelers holding notes could go a whole day without obtaining a single cash or article.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers with notes in hand could spend a whole day unable to obtain a single coin or good.

sentences.zh: 詔令侍從、台省，條上所見。

translations.literal: An edict ordered attendants and the censorate to submit their observations in detail.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered attendants and censors to submit detailed recommendations.

sentences.zh: 疇若奏曰：“物少則貴，多則賤，理之常也。

translations.literal: Chouruo memorialized: "When things are few they are dear; when many they are cheap—such is the constant principle."
translations.idiomatic: Chouruo memorialized, "When goods are scarce they are dear; when abundant they are cheap—such is nature's law."

sentences.zh: 曷若令郡縣姑以漸稱提，先收十一界者消毀，勿復支出。

translations.literal: How about ordering prefectures and counties for the time being to maintain value gradually, first collecting and destroying notes of the eleventh series and not issuing them again?
translations.idiomatic: Let prefectures and counties gradually restore note value: first collect and destroy notes of the eleventh series and issue no more.

sentences.zh: 上下流通，則不待稱提矣。

translations.literal: When above and below circulate freely, then there is no need to maintain value by decree.
translations.idiomatic: Once notes circulate freely above and below, enforced maintenance will no longer be needed.

sentences.zh: ”由是峻急之令少寬。

translations.literal: Because of this, harsh urgent orders were somewhat relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh enforcement was accordingly eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 又疏奏：“乞崇忠厚，延質樸，屏絕浮薄之論。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial: "I beg that loyalty and generosity be honored, simplicity and plainness be extended, and shallow frivolous discourse be barred."
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized, "Honor loyalty and generosity, welcome plain integrity, and bar shallow and frivolous talk."

sentences.zh: 乞撥買官田充糴本，以廣常平之儲。

translations.literal: I beg that funds be allocated to purchase official fields as capital for grain purchases, to expand Ever-Normal Granary reserves.
translations.idiomatic: Allocate funds to buy official fields as capital for grain purchases, to expand Ever-Normal Granary reserves.

sentences.zh: 乞令戶察一員，專監安邊所。

translations.literal: I beg that one revenue inspector be ordered to supervise exclusively the Bureau for Pacifying the Frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint one revenue inspector to supervise exclusively the Bureau for Pacifying the Frontier.

sentences.zh: ”帝皆是之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all of these.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all these proposals.

sentences.zh: 因麵求補外，退上章，降詔不允，又連疏丐去。

translations.literal: He asked in person for an outside appointment; returning, he submitted a memorial, and a gracious edict refused; he submitted successive memorials begging to leave.
translations.idiomatic: He asked in person for a provincial post; when refused by edict, he submitted repeated memorials begging to resign.

sentences.zh: 會旱蝗復熾，御筆令在朝百執事條上封事，疇若奏“官吏苛刻、科役頻並、賦斂繁重、刑法淹延”四事。

translations.literal: When drought and locusts flared again, the emperor's own brush ordered all officials at court to submit sealed memorials in detail. Chouruo memorialized on four matters: "harsh officials, frequent combined levies, heavy taxation, and delayed justice."
translations.idiomatic: When drought and locusts returned, the emperor ordered all officials to submit sealed memorials. Chouruo cited four ills: harsh officials, repeated combined levies, heavy taxation, and delayed justice.

sentences.zh: 冊皇太子，差充引見禮儀使。

translations.literal: At the investiture of the crown prince he was appointed to serve as commissioner for presentation ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: At the crown prince's investiture he was appointed commissioner for the presentation ceremony.

sentences.zh: 進華文閣待制、知成都府。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary at the Huawen Pavilion and appointed prefect of Chengdu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary at the Huawen Pavilion and made prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 蜀自吳曦畔後，製置使移司興元，朝論有偏重之嫌。

translations.literal: Since Wu Xi rebelled in Shu, the Pacification Commissioner moved his office to Xingyuan, and court opinion suspected undue bias.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wu Xi's rebellion in Shu, the pacification commissioner's office had moved to Xingyuan, and court opinion suspected undue favoritism toward the north.

sentences.zh: 朝廷擇人，故輟疇若以往，三辭不允。

translations.literal: The court chose a man and therefore released Chouruo to go; he declined three times but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The court chose him for the post; Chouruo declined three times but was not permitted to refuse.

sentences.zh: 避諱，改寶謨閣待制。

translations.literal: To avoid a tabooed name, his title was changed to Attendant-in-Ordinary at the Baomo Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: To avoid a tabooed name, his title was changed to Attendant-in-Ordinary at the Baomo Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 詔：“凡屬軍民利病，吏治藏否，並許諮訪以聞。

translations.literal: An edict said: "All matters affecting the welfare or harm of army and people, and whether official administration is sound or corrupt, are permitted to be inquired into and reported."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared, "You may inquire into all matters affecting soldiers and civilians, and report whether local administration is sound or corrupt."

sentences.zh: ”當征積欠十餘萬，疇若亟命榜九邑盡蠲之。

translations.literal: More than one hundred thousand in accumulated arrears were due for collection; Chouruo urgently ordered proclamations in nine districts to remit them entirely.
translations.idiomatic: When more than one hundred thousand in back taxes were due, Chouruo promptly ordered all nine districts to remit them entirely.

sentences.zh: 考官吏冗員，非敕命差注者悉罷之。

translations.literal: He examined officials for redundant posts; all not appointed by imperial order were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He reviewed officials for redundant posts and dismissed all not appointed by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 為民代輸六年布估錢，計二十萬二千四百緡；

translations.literal: He paid on the people's behalf six years of cloth appraisal levies, totaling two hundred two thousand four hundred strings;
translations.idiomatic: He paid six years of cloth appraisal levies on the people's behalf, totaling two hundred two thousand four hundred strings;

sentences.zh: 又別立庫儲二十五萬三千緡，期於異日接續代輸；

translations.literal: he also separately established a treasury reserve of two hundred fifty-three thousand strings, planning in future to continue paying on their behalf;
translations.idiomatic: established a separate reserve of two hundred fifty-three thousand strings for future payments on their behalf;

sentences.zh: 又糴米十五萬石有奇，足廣惠倉之儲；

translations.literal: he also purchased more than one hundred fifty thousand shi of rice, sufficient to fill the Broad Benefit Granary;
translations.idiomatic: purchased more than one hundred fifty thousand shi of rice to fill the Broad Benefit Granary;

sentences.zh: 又減他賦之重者，民力遂寬。

translations.literal: he also reduced other heavy levies, and the people's strength was thereby eased.
translations.idiomatic: and reduced other heavy levies, easing the people's burden.

sentences.zh: 初，沈黎蠻屢犯邊，疇若至，則鏤榜曉以禍福，青、彌兩羌遂乞降。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shenli tribesmen had repeatedly raided the frontier. When Chouruo arrived, he had engraved proclamations posted explaining fortune and misfortune, and the Qing and Mi Qiang tribes thereupon begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shenli tribesmen had repeatedly raided the frontier. Chouruo posted engraved proclamations explaining the consequences, and the Qing and Mi Qiang tribes submitted.

sentences.zh: 四年，董蠻合其部族入寇犍為利店。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Dong tribesmen united their clans and invaded Lidian in Qianwei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Dong tribesmen united their clans and attacked Lidian in Qianwei.

sentences.zh: 疇若亟調兵，且設方略捕之，皆遁去。

translations.literal: Chouruo urgently mobilized troops and devised stratagems to capture them; all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Chouruo urgently mobilized troops and laid plans to capture them; all fled.

sentences.zh: 先是，疇若廉知嘉定邊備廢弛，而平戎莊子弟可用，遂檄嘉定府權免平戎莊是年炭估、麻租，令莊子弟即日上邊為守備。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chouruo had secretly known that Jiading's frontier defenses were lax, while the young men of Pingrong Manor could be used. He therefore ordered Jiading Prefecture to temporarily exempt Pingrong Manor that year's charcoal appraisal and hemp rents, and commanded the manor's young men to go to the frontier that very day as defenders.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Chouruo had learned that Jiading's frontier defenses were lax and that the young men of Pingrong Manor could serve. He ordered Jiading to exempt the manor's charcoal and hemp levies for the year and sent its young men to the frontier at once as defenders.

sentences.zh: 會嘉定闕守，蠻窺利店無備，遂入寇。

translations.literal: It happened that Jiading lacked a magistrate; the tribesmen, seeing Lidian undefended, thereupon invaded.
translations.idiomatic: Jiading happened to lack a magistrate; the tribesmen, seeing Lidian undefended, invaded.

sentences.zh: 疇若復選西軍，欲且往防拓，牒轉運司折支，不報。

translations.literal: Chouruo again selected western troops and wished to go forthwith to defend the frontier; he sent a dispatch to the Transport Commission for advance payment, but received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Chouruo again selected western troops to defend the frontier and requested advance funds from the Transport Commission, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 蠻再犯龍鳩堡，轉運司始頗從所請。

translations.literal: The tribesmen again attacked Longjiu Fort; the Transport Commission only then largely granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribesmen attacked Longjiu Fort again, the Transport Commission at last largely granted his request.

sentences.zh: 蠻復到龍門隘，知有備乃退。

translations.literal: The tribesmen again reached Longmen Pass; learning there were preparations, they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen reached Longmen Pass again but withdrew on finding defenses ready.

sentences.zh: 進龍圖閣待制，依舊知成都府。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary at the Longtu Pavilion and continued as prefect of Chengdu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary at the Longtu Pavilion while remaining prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 大使司之師出，東路提刑亦征兵，三垂告警，敘南之報復急，兩路震動。

translations.literal: When the envoy commission's army marched out, the eastern-route judicial intendant also raised troops; the three frontiers sounded alarms; Xunan's reports of counterattack were urgent, and both routes were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy commission's army marched out and the eastern judicial intendant also raised troops, alarms sounded on three frontiers; urgent reports came from Xunan, and both routes were thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 疇若亟移書兩軍，俾速還師守險為後圖，西師遂退守沐川。

translations.literal: Chouruo urgently sent letters to both armies, ordering them to return quickly, hold the defiles, and plan for the future; the western army thereupon withdrew to defend Muchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chouruo urgently ordered both armies to withdraw, hold the defiles, and regroup; the western army retreated to defend Muchuan.

sentences.zh: 既而疇若兼製敘州兵甲公事，既得專行，益嚴守備，蠻首昔醜竟降，朝廷賞平蠻功，進疇若一秩。

translations.literal: Soon Chouruo concurrently directed military affairs of Xuzhou; once he could act on his own authority, he tightened defenses still further, and the tribal leader Xichou finally surrendered. The court rewarded the pacification of the tribesmen and advanced Chouruo one rank.
translations.idiomatic: Soon given sole charge of Xuzhou military affairs, he tightened defenses further until the tribal leader Xichou surrendered. The court rewarded the pacification and advanced Chouruo one rank.

sentences.zh: 疇若留蜀四年，弊根蠹穴，苗耨發櫛。

translations.literal: Chouruo remained in Shu four years, uprooting the roots of abuse and worm-eaten lairs, hoeing out seedlings and combing them forth.
translations.idiomatic: During four years in Shu, Chouruo rooted out entrenched abuses and exposed hidden corruption.

sentences.zh: 如乞揀留移屯西兵義勇，以防竊發，以救偏重；

translations.literal: Such as begging to select and retain western troops and militia moved to garrison posts, to guard against sudden outbreaks and remedy undue bias;
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retain western troops and militia at garrison posts to guard against sudden outbreaks and remedy the northward bias;

sentences.zh: 更用東南賢士使蜀四路，而拔蜀守之有治功者為東南監司，庶杜州縣姻婭之私；

translations.literal: to employ worthy men from the southeast in the four Shu circuits, and promote Shu magistrates with achievements in governance to be southeast circuit intendants, hoping thereby to stop private ties of kin and marriage in prefectures and counties;
translations.idiomatic: to send worthy men from the southeast to the four Shu circuits and promote effective Shu magistrates to southeast posts, hoping to end nepotism in local government;

sentences.zh: 輕取錢引貼期之費，以紓民力：皆抗疏請於朝，乞力行之。

translations.literal: to lighten collection of qianyin advance fees to ease the people's strength—all these he submitted in forthright memorials to the court, begging that they be vigorously carried out.
translations.idiomatic: and to reduce advance fees on paper currency to ease the people's burden—all submitted in forceful memorials begging the court to enact them vigorously.

sentences.zh: 復念大玄城乃張儀所築，高駢所修，圮壞歲久，復修費重，乃以節縮餘錢四十萬貫為修城備。

translations.literal: Again considering Great Xuancheng was built by Zhang Yi and repaired by Gao Pian, ruined for many years, rebuilding costly, thus used economized surplus money four hundred thousand strings as city-repair reserve.
translations.idiomatic: He also recalled that Great Xuancheng had been built by Zhang Yi and repaired by Gao Pian; after long ruin, rebuilding would be costly, so he set aside four hundred thousand strings of economized surplus funds as a reserve for repairing the walls.

sentences.zh: 疇若以製置使留漢中，則護諸將為得宜。

translations.literal: If Chou Ruo as military commissioner remained at Hanzhong, then protecting the various generals would be appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: If Chou Ruo were kept at Hanzhong as military commissioner, protecting the various generals would be the proper course.

sentences.zh: 召赴行在，入對延和殿，遷權兵部尚書、太子右庶子。

translations.literal: Summoned to the temporary capital, entered audience at Yanyhe Hall, promoted acting Minister of War, Right Senior Attendant to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the temporary capital, gave audience in the Yanyhe Hall, and was promoted to acting Minister of War and Right Senior Attendant to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 八年，四月不雨，詔求直言。

translations.literal: Eighth year, through the fourth month no rain, edict sought forthright speech.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, through the fourth month it did not rain, and an edict called for forthright advice.

sentences.zh: 疇若條具三事，首言：“比稱提楮幣，州縣奉行切迫，故因坐減陌被估籍者眾，乞與給還；

translations.literal: Chou Ruo enumerated three matters in detail, first saying: "Recently with increased valuation of paper currency, prefectures and counties enforced urgently, so many punished for reduced face value had property appraised and confiscated—beg to restore;"
translations.idiomatic: Chou Ruo set forth three matters in detail. First he said: "Recently, with the increase in value of paper currency, prefectures and counties enforced it urgently, so many who suffered reduced-face-value penalties had their property appraised and confiscated. I beg that these be restored;"

sentences.zh: 乞蠲閣下戶畸零稅賦；

translations.literal: beg to remit under-arcade households' irregular leftover taxes and levies;
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the irregular leftover taxes of under-arcade households be remitted;

sentences.zh: 乞振贍雄淮軍之乏。

translations.literal: beg to provide relief for the Xiong-Huai armies' shortages.
translations.idiomatic: and I beg that relief be provided for the shortages of the Xiong-Huai armies.

sentences.zh: ”尋皆行之。

translations.literal: " Soon all were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Soon all were implemented.

sentences.zh: 落權，升左庶子，仍兼修史，擢太子詹事。

translations.literal: Removed acting status, promoted Left Senior Attendant, still concurrently historiographer, elevated Chamberlain for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was relieved of his acting status, promoted to Left Senior Attendant, continued concurrently as historiographer, and was elevated to Chamberlain for the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 疇若引範鎮故事，乞歸田裏。

translations.literal: Chou Ruo cited Fan Zhen's precedent, begged to return to rural home.
translations.idiomatic: Chou Ruo cited Fan Zhen's precedent and requested to return to his rural home.

sentences.zh: 十年春，差知貢舉，試禮部尚書，以足疾乞歸。

translations.literal: Tenth year spring, dispatched to oversee metropolitan examination, tested as Minister of Rites, citing foot ailment begged to return.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the tenth year he was dispatched to oversee the metropolitan examination and was tested as Minister of Rites; citing a foot ailment, he requested to retire home.

sentences.zh: 進煥章閣學士、知福州，力辭，乃改提舉鴻慶宮。

translations.literal: Promoted Academician of Huanzhang Pavilion, appointed prefect of Fuzhou, firmly declined, then changed to director of Hongqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion and appointed prefect of Fuzhou, but firmly declined; he was instead made director of the Hongqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 關外軍潰，言者論及疇若，落職罷祠，後以煥章閣學士致仕。

translations.literal: Troops outside the pass routed, critics implicated Chou Ruo, demoted and stripped of sinecure, later retired as Huanzhang Pavilion Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When troops outside the pass routed, critics implicated Chou Ruo; he was demoted and stripped of his sinecure, and later retired as Academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 所著有《竹坡集》、奏議、講議、《經筵故事》。

translations.literal: Works authored include "Collection from Bamboo Slope," memorials, lecture notes, "Stories from the Classic Lectern."
translations.idiomatic: His works included the Collection from Bamboo Slope, memorials, lecture notes, and Stories from the Classic Lectern.

sentences.zh: 袁韶字彥淳，慶元府人。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao, styled Yanchun, native of Qingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao, styled Yanchun, was a native of Qingyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十四年進士。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year of Chunxi jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourteenth year of Chunxi.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰中，為吳江丞。
